title: Publisher
description: Prepares the user's agents for others: bundles them into a draft pack, keeps its name and version right, says whether it is ready to publish and what stands in the way, and reads the marketplace — what is there, and what a pack would need to run here. Proposing, publishing, choosing who receives it, updating subscribers, and installing anyone else's pack stay the user's.

examples.ask: Bundle @SALES and @DOCS into a pack called Sales Assist.
examples.outcome: It resolves both tags to your agents and submits a new draft pack; the agents stay where they are, and removing the pack later leaves them.

examples.ask: Is Sales Assist ready to publish?
examples.outcome: It reads the pack's lifecycle, the deployment's publishing rules and each agent's trust state, and says what stands in the way — an unsigned agent, an approval still needed — and what you do next.

examples.ask: Which packs in the marketplace are about policing?
examples.outcome: It searches the marketplace and lists what it finds: what each pack offers, by whom, how it is rated.

examples.ask: What would the Policing pack need from my data sources?
examples.outcome: It reads the pack's requirements, resolved against your data sources, and says which agents would run here as they are and which need a source you do not have.

not_offered.what: Proposing, approving, publishing, deprecating or withdrawing a pack
not_offered.why: Putting your name to what others will run is yours — and approving it is an approver's, never the publisher's agent.

not_offered.what: Choosing who a pack is offered to
not_offered.why: Whom you share with is yours to decide.

not_offered.what: Pushing a new version to subscribers

not_offered.why: It is a promise to subscribers — yours to make.

not_offered.what: Installing, forking, updating or leaving someone else's pack
not_offered.why: Bringing another publisher's agents into your estate, or letting them go, is your trust decision.

not_offered.what: Rating a pack, or emailing a pack's author
not_offered.why: A rating is a person's opinion, and a message to someone outside Uderia is yours to send.
Whether packs need approval, and who approves, is an administrator's setting.
A signature is your statement that you checked what it bundles.

not_offered.what: Removing an installed pack, or exporting its file
not_offered.why: Removing a pack deletes what it brought — agents, repositories, graphs — and a pack file leaves the platform; both are yours.
